name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: My hammer falls. The metal sings. Another sword begins to take shape. There is little cause for anything other than swords now. Every day, we hear word that the invaders grind closer, always whispered in hushed tones or written on the faces of the soldiers returning from battle. We smell it in the faint smoke on the eastern wind. We see it in defiant spirit of commonfolk gathering wood for palisades and digging trenches outside the gates. We feel it, all of us, in the invaders’ foul boots on our soil. In the weeks since their landing, they have taken mile upon mile of ground, and their black iron and blood-stained banners now stretch from the sea to our greatest cities. We know now that we do not have the strength to pry them from our shores. Not alone. And so, my hammer falls, and it shapes swords. All manner of hands come to claim them when they are ready: the calloused hands of the aged, the armored gauntlets of the fighting men. The slender fingers of fiery maidens, and the chalk-specked hands of the wise and learned. The smooth and eager hands of youths who should not yet aspire to take a life.

name: Name
body: The hands are always eager before they are bloodied. And bloodied they will be. A different hammer has fallen: a hammer made of bodies, ships, and engines of war, and the ringing of its impact echoes through the breadth of the Iron Kingdoms. The armies of Immoren bear the force of this hammer and the heat of its fire together. They are gathered just as pieces of iron, thrust into the heat of the forge and laid upon the anvil to receive blow after blow. Twisted and formed under violence, made pliable by unbearable flame, and struck again. Beaten. Folded. Fired. Again and again, until the metal becomes one, and a blade emerges. Or shatters under the hammer’s wrath. —Gerhard Dorgun, weaponsmith

name: Name
body: Black Tide Season 2, Chapter 1 is made up of three scenarios that should be played in order: "Piercing the Veil," "Monument to War," and "Signal Strength."

name: Name
body: As armies face off across the field of battle yet again, a biting chill falls across the landscape. Eerie mists grow on the stale wind, clouding eyes and twisting visions of the enemy. Both sides stumble in the fog and know in the back of their minds that this is not their enemy’s doing. Some outside force has chosen to intervene in this conflict, but the time for battle is at hand and the time for answers will have to wait.

name: Name
body:
Players fight to control a critical battlefield as a strange arcane presence meddles in the conflict, manifesting a dangerous and drifting fog that can aid or hinder, depending on how players navigate it.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Scenario 1 is suitable for 50- and 75-point games.

name: Name
body:
Place a large hill in the center of the battlefield and 2 objectives as indicated on the map below. Use tokens or dice to mark the six numbered points around the perimeter.
Players roll for first turn, with player 1 deploying first as indicated on the map and taking the first turn.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. After terrain has been placed, each player places one 3" cloud effect template on the battlefield within 1" of the center hill. These cloud effect templates represent the Rolling Fog.

name: Name
body: -Rolling Fog: At the beginning of each player turn, roll a d6 for each Rolling Fog template in play and move it 4" toward the corresponding numbered marker as indicated on the map. Rolling Fog templates that touch the edge of the board are removed from play. -Billowing Mist: Starting with the second turn, at the beginning of each of player 1’s turns, each player adds one Rolling Fog template to the battlefield. These templates must be placed within 1" of another Rolling Fog in play. If there are more than six Rolling Fogs on the battlefield at the beginning of player 1’s turn, do not add any more Rolling Fog templates. -Twisted Distortion: Rolling Fog templates are cloud effects. A model within one or more Rolling Fog templates suffers –1 AAT, –1 MAT, – RAT, and cannot Aim.

name: Name
body: Starting on the second round, at the beginning of each player’s turn, each player scores 1 Victory Point (VP) for each flag they secure and 2 VP if they hold the center hill uncontested.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any turn or the end of the sixth round, if a player secures both flags and holds the center hill uncontested, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At beginning of any turn, if a player has 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent, they win the match and receive 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest Points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: The invading forces have broken into the city, surging through streets and setting fires in their wake. Ahead, the outnumbered defenders rally at the city plaza to break the wave, a last and desperate stand in the shadow of one of their great heroes. As alarm bells ring throughout the city, the defenders dig in, hoping to hold out until reinforcements can arrive.

name: Name
body:
In this scenario, players clash at the site of a sacred monument, believed to be the divinely blessed protector of the city. Determined to break the spirit of the city’s people, the Invaders seek to desecrate the shrine by toppling its statues and capturing the heroic monument while the Defenders will stop at nothing to protect it.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: Scenario 2 is intended for 50-, 75-, and 100-point games

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, place a large obstruction (Monument) with a recommended size of 5" x 5" and 4 small objectives (Statues) on the battlefield.
Before deployment, the Defender may designate up to half their army’s points value to represent reinforcements. These units gain Ambush for this scenario. Only warrior models can be designated as reinforcements.
Invader models lose Ambush for this scenario.
The Invader takes the first turn in this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features. Urban terrain is recommended.

name: Name
body: -Blessed Shrine: Defender models within 5" of the Monument are immune to continuous effects. -Topple: An Invader Cohort model within 1" of a statue can topple it by doing the following: A medium- or larger-based horror within 1" of a statue can topple it by forfeiting its Normal Movement and Combat Action and spending one essence point. A medium- or larger-based warbeast within 1" of a statue can topple it by forfeiting its Normal Movement and Combat Action and being forced. A medium- or larger-based warjack within 1" of a statue can topple it by forfeiting its Normal Movement and Combat Action and spending one focus point. When a statue is toppled remove it from the battlefield. -Gobber Spy Mission: Players who include Reinholdt, Gobber Spy in their force can undertake the following covert missions: Defender: Pickpocket—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy can take Special Action: Pickpocket if within 2" of an Invader solo model. If so, the Defender receives 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action may only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body: Invader: Deface the Monument—Reinholdt, Gobber Spy can take Special Action: Deface if within 3" of the Monument. If so, the Invader receives 1 additional War Chest point for this scenario. This action may only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body:
The Invader scores 2 Victory Points each time they topple a statue.
Beginning on the second round, the Defender scores 1 VP for each statue they secure uncontested.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any turn or at the end of the sixth round, if two or more statues have been toppled and the Invader secures the Monument uncontested, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest Points. If no statues have been toppled and the Defender secures the Monument uncontested, at the end of sixth round, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any round, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: The signal tower looms overhead, a hundred feet of steel latticework capped in a hemisphere of copper and blue flashes of arcane electricity. It stands ready, setting the air to a vibrant hum, to send a word of warning through the skies that the invaders have arrived and a call of help to any that would stand in solidarity to repel them. But the unmistakable whine of its power coils is a call to the enemy, who leap to seize the brief window and stifle the message of hope before it can be sent.

name: Name
body: Players battle to control the titanic communications tower and its volatile power coils, the Defenders fighting to broadcast their message and the Invaders battling to shut down the tower for good.

name: Name
body: Scenario 3 is suitable for 50- and 75-point armies.

name: Name
body:
As shown on the map below, place a large obstruction (Communications Tower) in the center of the battlefield, with a recommended size of 5" x 5", and four objectives (Power Coils), centered on and 6" away from each side of the Communication Tower.
The Defender takes the first turn in this scenario.

name: Name
body: Players alternate placing terrain features, with each player placing up to 4 features.

name: Name
body: -Electric Arcs: If a model is directly hit by an AOE or spray attack within 4" of a Power Coil, all models within 4" of the Power Coil suffer a POW 10 electricity damage roll. -Ionization [4"]: When a model without Resistance: Electricity suffers an electrical damage roll while within 4" of one or more Power Coils, add +2 to the roll. - Ground: If a player secures the Communications Tower uncontested, during their Maintenance Phase, they can grant one model/unit Resistance: Electricity for one round.

name: Name
body: Starting on the second round, at the beginning of their turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point (VP) for each Power Coil they secure and 2 Victory Points if they secure the Communications Tower uncontested.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: At the beginning of any turn or at the end of the sixth round, if a player secures three of the four Power Coils and the Communications Tower uncontested, they win the match and receive 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any round, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
